parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented border friction, no facility or custody rule, and no visitor-facing universal exposure appear in the record. Constitutional and 2010 anti-discrimination protections expressly cover gender identity in services — traveller-relevant on paper — alongside a 2016 gender-recognition law (climate signal only). Offsetting: enforcement is weak (2017 ombudsman: LGBT murders uninvestigated, none sentenced), the 2024 survey documents widespread exclusion though LGBTI-wide, not trans- or visitor-specific, and the 2017 poll shows only slim majorities. Marriage recognition for a changed marker is unresolved (2017 supreme court invalidation, 2018 appeal outcome unknown), an open question rather than an exposure. Worst documented feature is tier 5 (paper protections not shown to operate) plus undated, non-patterned societal discrimination — reduced risk, but short of the operating-remedy acceptance tier.
